newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar closes firm, seen heading higher.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar closes firm, seen heading higher.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed firmer on Tuesday after trading a fairly tight range and dealers said expectations of further samurai bond issues would keep it well underpinned.
The New Zealand dollar closed at US$0.7091/98 and 67.76 on its Trade-Weighted Index, up from 0.7080/87 and 67.69 at the opening. It traded a 0.7078-96 range on the day.
A Wellington dealer said there were rumours of "yards and yards" of samurai issues still to come.
"We've seen some consistent selling of Kiwi out of Hong Kong, but local appetite, linked to rumoured forthcoming issues, has kept it underpinned," he said.

There was no firm news from latest coalition talks between the caretaker National Party government and the nationalist New Zealand First party, beyond a comment from Prime Minister Jim Bolger that progress was being made.

"We're all waiting for Friday's employment numbers," the dealer said. Ten economists polled by Reuters expect on average 0.2 employment growth in the September quarter following suprisingly strong growth of 0.9 percent in the June quarter.

An Auckland dealer said the New Zealand dollar could benefit from switching of funds out of Australia if the Reserve Bank there confirms a widely-expected 0.50 point cut in official rates on Wednesday to 6.50 percent.
The Kiwi firmed on the cross to A$0.9009/24 from 0.8992/06 at Monday's local close.
